definitions.gloss: Horyuji; ancient Buddhist temple in Nara
definitions.explanation: A Buddhist temple in Nara Prefecture founded in 607 by Prince Shotoku, home to what are considered the oldest surviving wooden buildings in the world, and registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

examples.japanese: {法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れた→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。
{法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{世界遺産|せかいいさん}→世界遺産：04897_sekaiisan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{登録|とうろく}→登録：05703_touroku⟧されている。
examples.english: Horyuji is registered as a World Heritage Site.

examples.japanese: {法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{五重塔|ごじゅうのとう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{世界最古|せかいさいこ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{木造建築|もくぞうけんちく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Horyuji's five-story pagoda is one of the oldest wooden structures in the world.

notes:
{法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ} in {奈良県|ならけん} (Nara Prefecture) was founded in 607 by Prince ⟦{聖徳太子|しょうとくたいし}→聖徳太子：16682_shoutokutaishi⟧ and is home to the world's oldest surviving wooden buildings, including its iconic five-story pagoda ({五重塔|ごじゅうのとう}).

CULTURAL NOTE:
In 1993 {法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ} became one of Japan's first UNESCO World Heritage Sites. It appears in one of Masaoka Shiki's most famous haiku, written while eating persimmons near the temple: 「⟦{柿|かき}→柿：04384_kaki⟧⟦{食|く}えば→食う：02657_kuu⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}るな→鳴る：01143_naru⟧り{法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ}」 ("I eat a persimmon, and the bell of Horyuji rings"), one of the best-known haiku taught in Japanese schools.
